v1.0.0 — the chain that stays: rules that change without a reset, a state root that scales, votes bound to their chain

**This release starts a new chain, and it is meant to be the last one.** From here on the rules
change through governance at a height everyone can see coming, not through a reset. Every operator
has to update and move the old chain data aside; balances and stakes of the old chain do not carry
over.

**Operators: how to update**

1. Stop your node.
2. In its data directory, rename — do not delete — `helix-data.redb` and `helix-peers.txt`
   (for example to `helix-data.redb.pre-v1.0.0`). **Keep `validator-key.json` and
   `validator-key.signing-state.json` where they are**: the key is your validator, and the
   signing state knows it belongs to the old chain and starts over on the new one by itself.
   In the desktop wallet, **Validate → Reset local chain** does this for you.
3. Install v1.0.0 and start the node. It joins the chain with genesis
   `GENESIS_HASH`, which is compiled in.
4. Wait until `helix chain status` (or `GET /status`) shows `peer_count` above zero and the height
   moving. Only then stake — a validator that is not connected cannot vote once it is active.
   **If you were validating when the test network ended** (`hlxk6QWX…`, `hlxRy5cA…`,
   `hlxSpsWWU…`), your validator address already holds 15,000 HLX from genesis. Stake from it, for
   example `helix tx stake 14000 --key validator-key.json`: the minimum is 10,000, the margin
   keeps a 5 % slash from dropping you out of the set, and the rest pays fees.
5. **Open your P2P port (8546 by default)** if you can, so other validators reach you directly.

**Rules change without a reset from now on**

- Stakers can schedule a protocol upgrade: `helix governance propose-upgrade <version>
  --at-height <height>`. Only the next version, activating after the proposal's voting period and
  at most 1,296,000 blocks (about 30 days) ahead. Once passed, the version and the height are part
  of the chain state.
- A node whose build supports the new version goes on under the new rules at that height. A node
  whose build does not stops cleanly at the block before it — it applies nothing more, proposes
  and votes nothing, keeps its data, and its API keeps answering — and says so: every minute
  beforehand with the blocks remaining, and at the height with what to install. Installing a
  release that supports the version is all it takes; it goes on from exactly where it stopped.
- `GET /status` and `GET /governance/params` name `protocol_version`,
  `supported_protocol_version` and `scheduled_upgrade`; the command line and the desktop wallet
  show a scheduled upgrade and warn when your node will not run it.

**What the chain commits to**

- The state root every block carries (`prev_state_root`) is a lattice hash over every entry of the
  state, the construction Solana commits its accounts with. A block costs what it changed: reading
  the root takes about 0.1 ms whether the chain holds a thousand accounts or a hundred thousand —
  before, every `/status` and every proposal rehashed the whole state (55 ms at 100,000 accounts).
  The set of active validators is part of it now.
- Votes and precommits are signed for one chain: a validator key that voted on another chain
  cannot have those votes counted here, and evidence of double signing has to come from this chain.
- Saving the state after a block writes the accounts the block changed, not every account
  (at 100,000 accounts: 18 ms and 36 KB per block, down from 545 ms and 3.9 MB).

**Genesis**

- 161,000 HLX: the bootstrap validator holds 15,000 staked — half again the minimum, so a slash no
  longer drops it out of the set — and 1,000 liquid for fees. The three operators validating at the
  end of the test network hold 15,000 each, as a balance they stake once their node is on the
  chain: a stake handed out at genesis would count in the quorum before their node is here. The
  other 100,000 are a launch reserve on `hlxf2ToZiQrv2XFAVvRgXU8ygDiH9TarQTuc`, whose key never
  touches a server. Every other coin is earned by producing blocks.
- A chain of your own (`HELIX_NEW_CHAIN=1`) starts the same way; to fund validators from its
  bootstrap validator, give it more at launch with `HELIX_GENESIS_VALIDATOR_LIQUID_HLX=<hlx>`.

**Desktop wallet**

- Governance proposals show their quorum and closing height again, and the "your node is catching
  up" banner appears again — both were lost between the node and the view.
- A scheduled protocol upgrade is shown as one, with the blocks remaining and a warning when the
  node beside the wallet will not run it.
